questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several things. I chose Berlin primarily because I like the city and really would love to try to live there for a while. Also, Freie Universität Berlin is on of the highest ranked universities in Political Science among the available Erasmus exchange universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many good things to say. I would however have loved to be in Berlin in the spring/summer semester. The winter in Berlin is pretty cold and grey. But it only fitted my study plan with an autumn/winter semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good information from Freie

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I wrote in a facebook-group with danes owning appartments in Berlin, and rented a small appartement in Kreuzberg.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great to be a part of the city of Berlin. I would really recommend to find a place to live in a nice area like Kreuzberg, Neukölln or Prenzlauer Berg

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy. Can't remember any trouble

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All I needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful. However, you need to or talk manually to some professors to get specific courses. But Freie guides you in the process, so I got all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to other students who have visited Freie to understand the ECTS-system - it is a bit complex. But other than that, just be there to the intro days and ask the Erasmus coordinators at Freie.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very different approach to Political Science - much more theory-based. Some courses better than others. But in general, competent and good professors and active students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot af talk and discussion. However also a bit 'fluffy sometimes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Banks and banking in global politics
Theories of workplace democracies
Democratic backsliding in US
Economic sociology and political economy: an introduction into the classics
Dynamics of protest politics
The semantics and politics of race

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Dynamics of protest politics. Nice research focused course focusing on the causes and effects of political protests. The course was organized in collaboration with Humbolt Universität, so you had classes with HU-students as well.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do any of the non-academic activites at Freie.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy Berlin. So many things to do and places to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Very open minded city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are open and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open minded and very liberal culture of Berlin.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The ECTS system is a bit wierd. But once you figure it out, its ok. Talk to fellow KU students who have been at Freie.

Search for appartements among the many danes who owns holiday-appartments in Berlin.

Choose a nice place to live. Don't care to much whether it is close to Freie or not. Transport in Berlin always take around 30-45 minutes no matter where you are and where you are going.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ECTS system at Freie - and also that the semester is a winter-semester from mid october to mid february.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in interesting city and being outside DK for a while. Also see another way to teach and study political science.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That the teaching ends in mid february and that there are exams afterwards. It is a bit difficult to fit in a KU semester structure. But it is possible.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
